introduction: Today, within the Octave of Christmas, we celebrate the Holy Family of Jesus, Mary and Joseph. Hannah brings her son Samuel to the house of the Lord and gives him to God. In the Gospel, Mary and Joseph search anxiously for the twelve-year-old Jesus and find him in the temple, in his Father's house. John reminds us that we are children of God. Let us pray for our families.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, see what love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God. Let us bring our families to him in prayer.
intentions: For the Church, the family of God: that she may be a home where everyone is welcomed and loved. Let us pray to the Lord.
For families, especially those under strain: that they may find in the Holy Family a model of love, patience and faith. Let us pray to the Lord.
For parents who are anxious about their children: that they may entrust them to God's care. Let us pray to the Lord.
For children and young people who are growing up: that they may increase in wisdom and in favor with God. Let us pray to the Lord.
For families who are separated, grieving or without a home: that God may comfort and protect them. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, you gave us the Holy Family as a model. Help our families to grow in love and faith, and bring us all at last to your home in heaven. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: In my Father's house
reflection.body:
The feast of the Holy Family reminds us that the Son of God grew up in an ordinary family, with its daily routines, its worries and its love.

The first reading tells of Hannah, who had longed for a child and prayed for one with tears. When Samuel is born, she names him and says, "Because I have asked him of the LORD." Later she brings him to the house of the Lord and gives him back to God: "I prayed for this child, and the LORD has given me my petition... Therefore I have also given him to the LORD." Every child is a gift, and every child ultimately belongs to God.

In the Gospel, the Holy Family goes up to Jerusalem for Passover, as they do every year. On the way home, Mary and Joseph realize that Jesus is not with them. Any parent can imagine their fear. After three days of searching, they find him in the temple, "sitting in the middle of the teachers, both listening to them and asking them questions."

Mary speaks with the honesty of a mother: "Son, why have you treated us this way? Behold, your father and I were anxiously looking for you." Jesus answers, "Didn't you know that I must be in my Father's house?" Mary and Joseph do not understand. Even the Holy Family lived with mystery and worry. Yet Jesus goes home with them to Nazareth: "He was subject to them." And Mary "kept all these sayings in her heart."

John tells us that God's love makes us all one family: "See how great a love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God!"

Today, pray for your family by name. If there is tension, take one step toward peace. And like Mary, keep in your heart the things you do not yet understand, and trust God with them.
